overview: A marine deuterostome phylum whose earliest robust atlas endpoint uses differentiated articulated faunas rather than isolated stereom or a contested Fortunian assignment.

ecology.diet: Diverse across the phylum; no ancestral diet inferred
ecology.locomotion: Sessile to mobile across sampled body plans
ecology.bodySize: Microscopic ossicles to large articulated bodies

traits: Multiple differentiated pentaradial and non-pentaradial body plans
evidenceSummary: Articulated faunas by about 510 Ma are robust; older isolated stereom and Yanjiahella’s proposed affinity are retained as separate evidence with explicit limits.

overview: The atlas separates Darriwilian total-group plates from a much younger modelled crown origin, so fossil occurrence and molecular divergence are not conflated.

ecology.diet: Omnivorous and detritivorous modes occur among living species; ancestral state unresolved
ecology.habitat: Marine benthic habitats from shallow to deep water
ecology.locomotion: Epifaunal and infaunal life modes; no single class-wide mode
ecology.bodySize: Not generalized by the cited global occurrence analysis

traits: Spines and tube feet in crown forms
Bothriocidaroid plates in the Ordovician stem record
evidenceSummary: Darriwilian plates support a total-group record; phylogenomics places crown Echinoidea around the Carboniferous–Permian boundary under model-dependent analyses.
